transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery and your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about your surgery or how you're getting on?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Yes, I have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So you should be fine to get back to that fairly soon.

However, you'll want to avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions for me?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

So you should be able to keep using your eye gel as you were before. Just make sure you store it as directed on the bottle - some need to be kept in the fridge and others at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.text: Yes, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery. It should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long has it been since your operation? That would help me give you a better idea of what to expect. But if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thanks for the information, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery!
